Subject: Orientation + hands-on prompt clinic — timezone matrix & final prep

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for agreeing to the POC orientation and hands-on prompt clinic next week. The goal for this session is to: 
- Surface the prompt inventory you currently use for search/autocomplete and the top 10 prompt flows you care about.
- Validate structured output requirements and routing rules (when to fall back to smaller models).
- Run a short load test (synthetic traffic) to confirm latency and KV-cache behavior for BrightCart's typical 2–3s user flows.

To make scheduling painless, can you confirm:
1) Which timezone most of your product team will join from (PST / EST / CET / IST)?
2) Do you prefer a single 3-hour block or two 1.5-hour blocks?
3) Who from your side will bring the prompt inventory CSV (we can accept a Drive link) and an SLA contact for load-test coordination.

I've attached a starter prompt inventory CSV and an agenda draft — feel free to edit. If it's helpful we'll send a short pre-read with guardrails and structured-output examples so we can focus on hands-on tuning during the session.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Samira / team —

Thanks for confirming. A few operational notes so load-test day goes smoothly:
- Load-test window: reserve a 45-minute window with an additional 15-minute warmup. We typically run synthetic traffic that matches your 90th-percentile token lengths.
- Routing checklist: please provide a short mapping (intent → model family) for the top 8 intents. If you have a boolean flag for ‘high-accuracy’ routes, call it out.
- KV-cache warmup: we will pre-seed the cache for the 20 minutes before the test; we need an API key scoped to the test dataset and network access from your staging VPC (if using private deployment).

Suggested concrete slots (two 1.5-hour blocks):
- Option A dates: Tue, Jun 22 & Wed, Jun 23 — 10:00–11:30 PT
- Option B dates: Thu, Jun 24 & Fri, Jun 25 — 08:30–10:00 PT

If Raj can confirm the staging endpoint and provide a short allowlist for our test IPs, we're good to schedule. I'm also attaching a quick runbook excerpt with the steps we'll take during the synthetic load test.
